article.headline: Manchester United Sacks Michael Carrick Following Worst Ever Premier League Season Start
article.summary: Manchester United has sacked head coach Michael Carrick after he oversaw only one win in 10 matches, leaving the club in the relegation zone.
article.body:
Michael Carrick’s departure came less than six months after he signed a two-year contract with the club. The decision was reached during a summit in Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified the move following recommendations from chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick had taken training on Wednesday, but his tenure ended the following morning after the hierarchy concluded a change was necessary to meet the club's ambitions.

This decision marks a critical turning point for a team that currently sits in the relegation zone after 10 league games. United’s management maintains that the current squad is significantly stronger than the results and performances displayed under Carrick. His exit follows a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, where the team conceded two goals within the first four minutes and trailed 4-2 early in the second half before staging a comeback. While that result and a win against Roma showed resilience, they were insufficient to secure Carrick’s future.

Sky Sports reports that Mauricio Pochettino has verbally agreed to replace Carrick as the next permanent manager. He is set to become the eighth permanent appointment since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013. Pochettino currently manages the USA national team and possesses a £7m release clause in his contract. United expects talks with the United Soccer Federation to accelerate shortly.

As the club searches for a permanent successor, internal changes are expected to continue, with coaching staff members Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate also anticipated to leave. Pochettino is expected to remain with the USA for their upcoming Nations League matches against Haiti this Saturday and Wednesday before potentially beginning his new role next Thursday.

article.headline: Over 700 Scottish schools hit by hoax bomb threats targeting students
article.summary: More than 700 schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received bomb threats that authorities have assessed as non-credible hoaxes.
article.body:
More than 6,000 schools in Italy also faced similar warnings, bringing the total number of affected institutions to thousands across three regions. Despite the scale of the emails, authorities in all locations confirmed there is no concrete danger or risk to the public. In Scotland, the messages specifically referenced a figure named Mikhail Andropov and identified as the leader of a project called Red Owl. While some local authorities chose to evacuate buildings as a precaution, Police Scotland explicitly stated that there is no requirement to keep children away from classrooms based on the email content alone.

These threats create significant disruption for parents, pupils, and staff who must manage the stress of unexpected warnings during the school day. While police are investigating the origins of the messages, the incidents are being treated as part of a wider trend that has recently affected hospitals, supermarkets, and airports across Europe. Officials are currently working to determine if these events are connected to other international hoaxes, though early indications point to a coordinated strategy intended to incite alarm rather than cause physical harm.

Scottish Education Secretary Mairi McAllan confirmed that specialist cyber-crime officers are actively working to identify the source of the communication. Meanwhile, in Northern Ireland, education officials have advised schools to continue normal operations unless specifically directed otherwise by police. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated on social media that the threats lack evidence of real danger, describing the strategy as an attempt to cause concern rather than a genuine security breach. Investigators continue to monitor the situation to ensure the safety of students and staff across the affected regions.

news.og_desc: En Estados Unidos, un vuelo que trasladaba a inmigrantes iraníes deportados a Irán, vía Pakistán, fue abruptamente cancelado el domingo por la mañana, cuando al menos ocho iraníes ya habían sido subidos a un avión con destino a la República de Georgia en la ciudad de Mesa, estado de Arizona. Según se informa, esta habría sido la primera deportación de ciudadanos iraníes desde que Estados Unidos dio inicio a sus ataques contra Irán en febrero.
